description: Vellum is a declarative artifact emitter: a specification of generic blocks in, a document out. It emits DOCX, XLSX, PPTX and PDF/A-2b from one model, and fills existing OOXML templates without disturbing the parts it does not understand. Identical inputs produce byte-identical outputs. Vellum never renders a chart, never performs network I/O, and never runs an external binary.

formats.name: docx
formats.note: A flowing document. Word paginates it, so Vellum does not compute page breaks.

formats.name: xlsx
formats.note: Presentation tables, not a spreadsheet: no formulas, no pivot tables, no macros. A consumer wanting a live model builds it elsewhere.

formats.name: pptx
formats.note: A deck. The only format with a native speaker-note channel, and the only one where Vellum computes the overflow split itself.

formats.name: pdf
formats.note: PDF/A-2b, emitted directly rather than converted. Every font is embedded, because the archival profile requires it.

blocks.purpose: A titled division of the content. Level 1 is the most prominent.
An artifact the host resolves by handle. Vellum embeds it; it never renders one. Ask Boxes what size to render at.
An analytical table: hierarchical headers on both axes, annotations attached to values, margins distinguishable from data.
Starts a new page, slide or sheet, depending on the format.
Annotation content. Native in a deck; a footnote or a cell comment elsewhere, as the capability matrix declares.

capabilities.note: A flowing document has no speaker-note channel, so a note becomes a footnote anchored where the block sits.

capabilities.degrade: raster fallback with the vector embedded alongside
capabilities.note: Word 2016 and later read an SVG only when a raster blip accompanies it. The caller supplies the pair; Vellum will not rasterise, because it never renders.
The asset becomes a package part verbatim and Word decodes it, so every encoding variant of an accepted media type passes through untouched.
Carried as the drawing's descr attribute, which is what a screen reader announces.

Font embedding in OOXML is a document-settings feature Vellum does not author in v1, so a theme's faces are referenced by name and the reader resolves them. Degrades rather than rejects because a theme that merely permits embedding should still render; a theme that explicitly demands it gets VELLUM_FONT_EMBED_UNSUPPORTED instead, because an explicit demand is a statement about a licence and must not be silently downgraded.
As above.
The family is referenced by name and the application resolves it, which is what every face gets in v1.
The outline format does not change the answer here, because this format embeds no font programs in v1: every face is referenced by name whatever its outlines are.
Vellum writes the characters and the application lays them out. It does no shaping or line breaking for this format, so it imposes no restriction on the writing system.
A flowing format paginates itself. Vellum does not lay out OOXML, and a split it computed would disagree with the one Word performs.

capabilities.degrade: a styled cell above the table
capabilities.note: A sheet has no heading construct; the text occupies a cell.
Declared unsupported rather than approximated. A workbook is where a reader goes for the numbers behind a chart, not for the chart.

capabilities.degrade: text appended to the cell, with the typed value preserved in a neighbouring column
capabilities.note: A cell holds one typed value. Appending the annotation to the number would turn it into text and defeat the reason to export a workbook at all.
This format takes no assets at all, so the encoding variant never arises. The row exists so the answer is a lookup rather than an inference from a missing cell.
As DOCX: xlsx references a family by name and never carries the program.
As above.
The outline format does not change the answer here, because this format embeds no font programs in v1: every face is referenced by name whatever its outlines are.
Vellum writes the characters and the application lays them out. It does no shaping or line breaking for this format, so it imposes no restriction on the writing system.
A sheet has no page, so a long table simply continues.
The only format with a native speaker-note channel.

capabilities.degrade: raster fallback with the vector embedded alongside

capabilities.note: Carried as the drawing's descr attribute, which is what a screen reader announces.
As DOCX. A deck is the case where a missing face is most visible, because a slide's type is large and its layout is fixed — which is why the substitution is warned rather than assumed harmless.
As above.
The outline format does not change the answer here, because this format embeds no font programs in v1: every face is referenced by name whatever its outlines are.
Vellum writes the characters and the application lays them out. It does no shaping or line breaking for this format, so it imposes no restriction on the writing system.
A table longer than a slide continues onto the next with its headers repeated. Capacity is theme-derived rather than measured, so the split is reproducible.
A PDF annotation would be closer in spirit but is not guaranteed visible in every reader, and PDF/A restricts annotation types. A footnote is legible everywhere.

PDF has no SVG mechanism. Vellum will not rasterise, because it never renders, and will not ship an SVG-to-PDF translator, which would be a second renderer with its own text layout and font matching, free to drift from whatever produced the asset. Supply a raster, or ask Boxes what size to render at.

The alpha channel becomes an /SMask, which PDF/A-2 permits and PDF/A-1 did not — one of the reasons the target is 2b. It is the one PNG form whose colour samples are rebuilt rather than passed through, because PNG interleaves alpha with colour in the same scanline and PDF keeps them in two streams. The pixels are unchanged; only the arrangement is.

Adam7 reorders the pixels into seven passes, which no PDF filter describes. De-interlacing means fully decoding the image and recompressing it — changing the bytes a consumer supplied, silently, to work around how they chose to save the file. Save it non-interlaced instead.

DCTDecode is defined over baseline and extended sequential JPEG. Progressive is legal JPEG that a conforming PDF reader is not obliged to decode, so embedding it produces a file that opens in the reader it was tested against and shows a blank frame in the next one. Refused rather than accepted on the strength of one reader.

An accessible description needs somewhere to attach, and in PDF that is the structure tree — which PDF/A-2b does not require and Vellum does not write. A bare /Alt on a marked-content sequence is legal and no reader surfaces it, so writing one would satisfy a checker and help nobody. Tagged output is PDF/A-2a and 2u, which is a different conformance level and a different piece of work. Warned rather than dropped silently, because the description is content the consumer wrote.

A DeviceCMYK image needs a CMYK output intent for the file to stay PDF/A conforming, and Vellum ships one intent: sRGB. Converting CMYK to RGB is a colour management decision with no single right answer, and making it silently would change the colours a consumer chose. Supply RGB or greyscale.
PDF/A-2b requires every font embedded, and TrueType outlines are subsetted. A face with CFF outlines cannot be subsetted; see font.outlines.cff, which is where that answer lives.
The whole program is embedded, which is what the theme asked for. A licence forbidding subsetting is the usual reason to ask.

capabilities.degrade: the regular cut of the same face
capabilities.note: A PDF names one font program per face, and a theme in v1 declares one program per role — so there is no bold cut to select. An OOXML target sets a flag and lets the application find or synthesise one; Vellum will not synthesise here, because a stroked outline is a different shape from a designed bold and passing it off as one is a fidelity claim Vellum cannot make. Warned rather than dropped silently. Give the theme a face per weight, or compose to an OOXML target.

capabilities.degrade: the upright cut of the same face
capabilities.note: As text.bold, and for the same reason. A sheared upright is not an italic: a true italic redraws letterforms rather than slanting them, and the difference is exactly what a reader notices.

PDF/A-2b requires every font embedded, so a face the theme declared non-embeddable cannot be used here at all — there is nothing to embed and referencing the family by name would produce a document whose appearance depends on what is installed where it is opened, which is the opposite of archival. This is the row that decides a theme is usable for PDF, and it is why the built-in theme is not: its three faces are all declared non-embeddable, because Vellum ships no font program. Supply a theme whose faces carry handles your asset resolver can serve.

capabilities.degrade: the whole font program embedded rather than a subset
capabilities.note: Vellum subsets glyf and not CFF: a CFF subsetter means a second outline format and a charstring interpreter, and the size it saves is not worth the ways it can be subtly wrong. The face is embedded whole and the document is conforming. A theme demanding embed: "subset" of a CFF face gets VELLUM_FONT_EMBED_UNSUPPORTED rather than this degradation, because subset-only may be a licence condition and must never be silently ignored.

Vellum lays PDF out itself, so it can only promise the systems it has established it shapes and breaks correctly: horizontal left-to-right Latin, Greek and Cyrillic in v1. Anything else is refused at compose time rather than rendered wrong — an unsupported script does not fail to draw, it draws incorrectly, and that is a defect a reader of the language finds and a test does not. Two supported systems mixed in one string is also refused, for the same reason. Compose to an OOXML target, which does its own layout.
Vellum paginates PDF itself, so the policy is honoured exactly.
Fill mode edits an OPC package surgically. A PDF is not one, and editing PDF in place is a different problem with none of the same guarantees.

operations.name: validate
operations.summary: Check a specification against a format's capability matrix. Reports every rejection at once.

operations.name: capabilities
operations.summary: Return the feature-by-format matrix, so a scheduled job can learn what will happen before it runs.

operations.name: schema
operations.summary: Return the published JSON Schema for a specification.

operations.name: hash
operations.summary: Return a specification's content hash. Derived from inputs, so an artifact's identity is knowable before it is produced.

operations.name: boxes
operations.summary: Return the asset slots a theme declares for a format, so a host knows what size to render an asset at. Answerable before a specification exists.

operations.name: compose
operations.summary: Render a specification to a format.

operations.name: inspect
operations.summary: Report a template's anchor inventory and font requirements without modifying it.

operations.name: fill
operations.summary: Bind data into an OOXML template, leaving every part it did not touch byte-identical.
